What You’d Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item A4 is a stainless hex head cap screw with two features you can spot before you ever read the print: the large flat washer that stays on the screw, and the green patch on the threads.

As received: stainless hex head screws with the captive flat washer and the green adhesive patch on the threads, shown on a millimeter grid.

Plain Stainless Finish — no plating or color coating on the metal. Item specification: Finish = Plain; the print adds bright passivation only.

Green Scotch-Grip Patch — pre-applied adhesive on the thread. The adhesive activates on assembly, bonding the external thread to the internal thread of the nut or tapped hole, which keeps the parts from loosening in vibration.

Hex Head — external hex drive on a DIN 933 hex head cap screw, fully threaded to the head.

Captive Flat Washer (SEMS) — a large flat stainless washer assembled onto the screw, so the two ship and install as one piece. The print lists it as a stainless flat washer, DIN 6902.

Topic T4 · Material Selection

A2-80 Stainless Steel

The second “S” in .8C30MHSS8/SGP calls out the base material, and the “8” right after it gives the grade. Here’s what that actually means on the shop floor.

Requirement

Material: stainless steel (18-8 / A2 family) · Screw grade: A2-80 · Washer grade (per print): A2-70

What “18-8” Means

18-8 is an American term for a common grade of stainless steel containing 18% chromium and 8% nickel.

What A2-80 Means

A2 is the 18-8 (type 304) stainless family. The number is the strength class — the minimum tensile strength in MPa divided by 10, so A2-80 ≈ 800 MPa. That is a higher strength class than A2-50 or A2-70.

Equivalent Grade

The A2 family is equivalent to type 304 stainless steel.

Screw vs. Washer

On the print the screw is A2-80 while its flat washer is A2-70, so the two pieces of the assembly are not the same strength class.

Corrosion Resistance

Good corrosion resistance in typical service environments.

Why It Matters

18-8 is the default stainless callout across most of SBS’s fastener line, which keeps sourcing and lead times predictable.

The print’s own material callouts — look at the two MAT’L columns on the highlighted row: screw A2-80, washer A2-70. SBS’s materials cross-reference: Material Conversion tool ↗

Topic T5 · Surface Treatment

Plain Finish, Bright Passivation

There is no finish code in .8C30MHSS8/SGP — the part is a plain stainless screw. The print still calls for one coating on the screw and washer: bright passivation.

Requirement

Item finish: Plain. Print coating for the screw and washer assembly (250000966): Type 2-A, bright passivation.

Typical Call-Out

Table #2 lists 2-A (bright passivation) and 2-B (passivation per ASTM A967-05 Nitric 1 or QQ-P-35C Type 2).ASTM A967 and QQ-P-35C are the standards that govern passivation of stainless steel parts.

Print Table #2 — the 2-A row (outlined) is the coating called out for this assembly.

Meaning

Passivation is a chemical clean-up of the stainless surface: it removes free iron picked up during machining and forming, so the steel’s natural corrosion resistance can do its job. It is not a plated or painted layer, so the part still reads as “Plain” in the item specification.

What Passivation Actually Is
  • A chemical treatment (typically acid-based) applied to stainless steel after the part is made.
  • Because it only cleans and restores the surface, it does not add meaningful thickness or change the part’s dimensions or thread tolerance.
  • “Bright” passivation keeps the metal’s natural, shiny stainless appearance.
  • The print gives 2-A no separate specification or notes (both read N/A); 2-B, by contrast, names ASTM A967-05 or QQ-P-35C.
Why It Matters — and Where It Shows Up

Corrosion Performance

Passivated stainless is intended for service where the fastener will see moisture and weather. This part ships to the same customer family that approves its patch adhesive, so the finish is controlled by print, not left to chance.

Clean, Uncoated Look

No color or plating means the washer and head keep the plain stainless look you see in the as-received photo; the only color on the part is the green thread patch.

Learn more in SBS’s own guide: Platings and Coatings ↗

Topic T6 · Extra Thread Locking Treatment

The Green Scotch-Grip Patch

The “/SGP” suffix calls out a pre-applied adhesive patch on the threads, supplied per the print.

Requirement

With heavy green Scotch-Grip 3M 2353 + 2353Y, or heavy turquoise ND Microspheres 593S (as per global BRP deviation), per print # 203000573 Rev A.BRP: a customer of SBS’s (Bombardier Recreational Products). ND 593S is the alternate adhesive allowed under the BRP deviation.

(1) 3M Scotch-Grip 2353 Heavy

Green color. Print type 1-A: “3M 2353 Heavy, green color, or equivalent approved by BRP.”

(2) ND 593S Microspheres

Heavy turquoise. Accepted as an alternate under the global BRP deviation named in the item description.

The Standard Behind It

Table #1 sets type 1-A “as per standard: IFI-525 1996 + 50%.” The “+ 50%” is part of the print callout; check the print with Engineering for how it is applied.IFI-525: the Industrial Fasteners Institute standard for this type of metric adhesive-coated thread patch.

How a Thread Locker Stops Vibrational Loosening

  1. The problem. Vibration makes the mating threads slip sideways by tiny amounts. Each slip lets the screw turn back a little, clamp load drops, and the joint works loose.
  2. The patch activates on assembly. As the screw is driven in, the pre-applied adhesive is crushed between the external and internal threads and fills the gap.
  3. The bond holds. Once cured, the adhesive bonds the threads together and resists turning, so the fastener keeps its clamp load under vibration.
The green patch on the threads of the finished part (reference photo).
The Patch on the SBS Website
SBS’s own Pre-Applied Patches guide, covering nylon patches and thread lockers. Explore Pre-Applied Patches and Adhesives ↗
With vs. Without a Locking Patch

Without a Locking Patch

Usage — a standard threaded fastener: only the machined thread fit holds the joint.

Effectiveness — gaps remain between the threads, so vibration lets them slip, the screw backs off, clamp load drops and the joint can work loose.

With a Locking Patch (/SGP)

Usage — the patch is pre-applied to the threads and activates as the screw is driven in, with no separate locker to apply at assembly.

Effectiveness — the adhesive fills the gaps and, once cured, bonds the threads and resists turning, so the fastener keeps its clamp load under vibration.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and standard used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term’s “jump” button to see it in context.

A2-80 Stainless Steel

A2 is the 18-8 (type 304) stainless family; “18-8” is the American term for stainless steel with 18% chromium and 8% nickel. The number is the strength class: the minimum tensile strength in MPa divided by 10, so A2-80 is about 800 MPa. On this part the screw is A2-80 and the flat washer is A2-70 per the print.

Bright Passivation

A chemical treatment that cleans free iron from the surface of stainless steel so its natural corrosion resistance can work, while keeping the metal’s shiny appearance. It does not add a plated layer. It is coating type 2-A on this part’s print.

BRP

Bombardier Recreational Products — one of SBS’s customers. A “BRP deviation” is a substitution approved specifically for their orders, not a change to the part in general.

DIN 933

The German standard for hexagon head screws that are threaded all the way to the head — the head shape and thread style this part is built to.

IFI-525

The Industrial Fasteners Institute standard covering metric adhesive-coated (pre-applied patch) screws — the standard named for the thread patch in print Table #1.

ND Microspheres 593S

An alternate pre-applied adhesive patch (heavy turquoise on this part) that the item description allows as per the global BRP deviation.

Scotch-Grip

The 3M brand name of the adhesive thread-locking patch pre-applied to this part’s threads — the heavy green version here.

SEMS

A screw supplied with its washer already assembled and captive on it, so the two install as one piece. The first “S” after “MH” in the part number marks this.

VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)

A bin system where SBS manages and restocks parts directly at the customer’s location. This training module is named after Item A4’s cell on the VMI bin card.
